source: E-mem: Multi-Agent Based Episodic Context Reconstruction
summary: ICML 2026 paper proposing episodic context reconstruction via a master agent coordinating multiple assistant agents that hold uncompressed memory contexts, arguing this outperforms compression-based memory methods for causal chains.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — interesting architecture, but AgentForge already ships skill distillation + planner injection. Run-outcome episodic memory is explicitly tracked by open issue HID-188; creating a new issue would be a theme-level duplicate.

summary: NeurIPS 2026 paper treating budget as a live control signal via progressive interval estimation; reports frontier models are over-optimistic and keep spending on tasks they're unlikely to finish.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — directly relevant to cost management, but Phase 2 explicitly prohibits proposing budget/timeout optimizers before HID-163 (token telemetry) ships. Backlog is also at >=10, blocking new issues.

source: INTENT: Inference-Time Planner with Cost Lookahead (arXiv 2602.11541)
summary: An inference-time planner that uses a learned world model to forecast tool usage and cost via Monte Carlo lookahead, enforcing hard budget feasibility without retraining.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — interesting cost-aware planning pattern, but prerequisite HID-163 must ship first before any budget-enforcement mechanism makes sense. Explicitly deferred per Phase 2 notes.

source: pi-reflect: Session-end reflection loop editing CLAUDE.md rules
summary: ~900-line TypeScript MIT-licensed tool that runs after each session and edits the agent's markdown rules file (AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md) based on friction detected in past sessions.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low-Medium — AgentForge already ships skill distillation into planner prompts (distillationAgent.ts, agentSkillRepository.ts). HID-188 covers cross-run episodic memory. The gap this closes is executor prompts not receiving skills yet, but that is a small delta from existing capability rather than a new paradigm.

summary: Claude Code plugin that runs autonomous improvement cycles (discover, build, audit, ship) on any codebase with eval gating and continuous learning; created March 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge's skill distillation already captures learned patterns from runs. evolve-loop's approach of modifying the codebase itself is out of scope for an orchestrator. The eval-gating pattern is interesting but already partially covered by HID-135 (synthesize acceptance-test harness).

source: LangGraph 1.2 — per-node timeouts, DeltaChannel, per-interrupt IDs
summary: LangGraph 1.2 (May 2026) adds per-node timeouts, error handlers, graceful shutdown, DeltaChannel for incremental state updates, and per-interrupt IDs for resuming after interruptions; at v1.2.20 as of late October 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge uses a custom Fastify state machine, not LangGraph. The per-node timeout pattern is conceptually relevant to stage-level timeouts, but HID-167 (automatic retry with failure classification) already covers subprocess failure handling. No gap opened by this release.

summary: Microsoft shipped Agent Framework 1.0 for Python and .NET in April 2026, moving AutoGen into maintenance mode (bug fixes only). It is now the recommended multi-agent path for Microsoft ecosystem projects.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge is Node.js/TypeScript with its own state machine; migrating to or integrating Microsoft Agent Framework is out of scope.

source: Karpathy 'Claws' concept and agentic engineering commentary
summary: Karpathy proposed 'Claws' (personal-hardware agent layer adding orchestration, scheduling, tool calls, persistence atop LLMs) and coined 'agentic engineering' (humans own architecture and correctness, agents own code volume). No shipped product.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — philosophical framing, not an implementable pattern. His autoresearch project reached 66k stars but details are sparse and it's a research tool, not an orchestration framework.

summary: OpenAI Agents SDK absorbed Swarm and is now the OpenAI-native multi-agent option; v0.12.1 from March 2026, shipping multiple releases per week. Python-only, OpenAI API-first.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge uses Claude Code and Codex CLI subprocesses, not OpenAI API clients. Framework is Python-only and API-based, incompatible with AgentForge's CLI subprocess architecture.
